title: Microsoft Purview: permanently delete OneDrive and SharePoint files with Priority cleanup (Worldwide)
summary: The controls, licensing statements, default and rollout dates are supported by Microsoft documentation and the supplied records. Minor corrections would complete two navigation paths and cite the sibling roadmap records; no actionable factual errors were found.

claims.claim: The static permanent-deletion creation route is Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > + Create a priority cleanup > Choose the type of priority cleanup > Static > Policy for SharePoint/OneDrive > Choose what to do with the content > Delete data permanently.
claims.quote: On the Choose what to do with the content page, select Delete data permanently. [Linked prerequisites page:] For Static scope, select Policy for SharePoint/OneDrive and then select one or more of the locations for sites and OneDrive accounts.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a command or API that creates a Priority cleanup policy with the permanent-deletion option.
claims.quote: Searched: Priority cleanup permanent deletion PowerShell New-ComplianceTag Set-RetentionCompliancePolicy New-RetentionComplianceRule PriorityCleanup. Read the permanent-deletion page and those cmdlet search excerpts; none describes setting the permanent-deletion option.

claims.claim: The tenant creation switch is at Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup settings > Configuration > control for priority cleanup in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management. From the top right, select Priority cleanup settings. From the Configuration page, turn off the control for priority cleanup, and select Save.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented PowerShell or an API for the tenant Priority cleanup creation switch.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell Priority cleanup tenant enable disable configuration switch permanent deletion. Read results and the SharePoint/OneDrive tenant-switch section; only the portal control was documented.

claims.claim: Permanent-deletion approval is at Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > Pending cleanups > cleanup > Approve disposal in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Select the cleanup and review the identified items, their locations, and their history. Select the items to delete, and then select Approve disposal.
claims.fix: In the front matter and rendered table, replace the path with 'Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > Pending cleanups > cleanup > items > Approve disposal' to include selecting the items to which approval applies.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented PowerShell or an API for approving Priority cleanup disposal.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com Priority cleanup Approve disposal PowerShell Microsoft Graph API disposition. Read results, the permanent-deletion approval instructions and SharePoint/OneDrive approval section; no applicable approval operation was documented.

claims.claim: The cleanup ID for monitoring is reached through Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > policy details.
claims.quote: Go to Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup and open the policy details. Copy the cleanup ID.
claims.fix: In the front matter and rendered table, replace the path with 'Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > policy details > Copy the cleanup ID'. The existing path reaches the right page but stops before the documented copy action.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <start> -EndDate <end> -Operations PriorityCleanupFileDeleted -FreeText <cleanup ID> searches deletion events for the cleanup ID.
claims.quote: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -EndDate <ExDateTime> -StartDate <ExDateTime> [-FreeText <String>] [-Operations <String[]>]. The FreeText parameter filters the log entries by the specified text string. The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Priority cleanup has an additional Delete data permanently option for targeted SharePoint and OneDrive files.
claims.quote: Permanent deletion is an additional option for a Priority Cleanup policy. On the Choose what to do with the content page, select Delete data permanently.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Permanent deletion bypasses the SharePoint and OneDrive recycle bins.
claims.quote: This option bypasses the SharePoint and OneDrive recycle bins.

claims.claim: Permanently deleted content is no longer discoverable in SharePoint search.
claims.quote: After deletion, the content is no longer discoverable in SharePoint search, Microsoft 365 Copilot, or eDiscovery.

claims.claim: Permanently deleted content is no longer discoverable in Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: After deletion, the content is no longer discoverable in SharePoint search, Microsoft 365 Copilot, or eDiscovery.

claims.claim: Permanently deleted content is no longer discoverable in eDiscovery, subject to the separately stated review-set exception.
claims.quote: After deletion, the content is no longer discoverable in SharePoint search, Microsoft 365 Copilot, or eDiscovery. Items already copied to an eDiscovery review set aren't deleted by Priority Cleanup.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Priority cleanup can override retention settings.
claims.quote: Permanent deletion can override retention settings or eDiscovery holds.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup can override eDiscovery holds after the required approval.
claims.quote: Permanent deletion can override retention settings or eDiscovery holds. Deleting items subject to legal holds requires explicit administrator approval for disposition.

claims.claim: The standard Priority cleanup workflow moves identified items to the second-stage Recycle Bin.
claims.quote: Use the standard Priority Cleanup workflow when you want identified items to move to the second-stage Recycle Bin.

claims.quote: Enter the policy name and description, choose an adaptive or static scope, select the SharePoint or OneDrive locations, and define the query for the targeted files.

claims.quote: select the SharePoint or OneDrive locations, and define the query for the targeted files.

claims.quote: Choose whether to delete matched items as soon as possible or prevent deletion until a set time.

claims.quote: Assign the required approvers. Run the policy in simulation mode and review the returned samples.

claims.quote: Run the policy in simulation mode and review the returned samples. After the simulation results are satisfactory, have a second Priority Cleanup admin review the results and turn on the policy.

claims.claim: The roadmap description says retention policies and labels keep deleted SharePoint and OneDrive content in recycle bins for 93 days.
claims.quote: M365 retention labels policies and M365 retention policies do not hard delete content immediately and keeps the data in Recycle Bins for 93 days for ODSP.

claims.claim: The roadmap description identifies data spillage as a Priority cleanup use case.
claims.quote: Priority Cleanup feature allows users to bypass retention, and eDiscovery holds to help customers comply to changing legal/compliance requirements or manage data spillage scenarios.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice positions the feature as reducing exposure from growing Copilot-related content such as Teams transcripts.
claims.quote: This capability helps reduce data exposure risk from rapidly growing Copilot-related content. Review your organization’s data risk and retention strategy, especially for Copilot-generated content such as Teams transcripts.

claims.where: Why it matters; summary; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft's notice says user workflows do not change unless an administrator configures and applies a policy.
claims.quote: There is no change to user workflows unless an admin configures and applies a priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: The tenant-level Priority cleanup capability is enabled by default.
claims.quote: Because of the built-in safeguards, the feature itself is enabled by default at the tenant level.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive Priority cleanup requires simulation at least once.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive, you must run simulation at least one time, and for any change other than the policy description.

claims.claim: Learn says review-set data is automatically deleted when an eDiscovery administrator deletes the entire case.
claims.quote: This data is automatically deleted when the entire eDiscovery case is deleted by an eDiscovery admin.

claims.claim: Learn's overview says Priority cleanup can override Preservation Lock when retention settings are delete-only.
claims.quote: Because the deletion from priority cleanup can override existing holds and even Preservation Lock when the retention settings are for delete-only

claims.claim: The same Learn page's Limitations section says those Preservation Lock items are not in scope outside simulation.
claims.quote: In simulation mode, items under preservation lock where the retention settings are configured for delete-only may show up. These items are not actually in scope for priority cleanup outside simulation mode.

claims.claim: Learn documents multiple approvals, specific roles and auditing as safeguards.
claims.quote: the process requires multiple approvals, specific roles, and is audited.

claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Admin is required to create and manage the policy.
claims.quote: Assign the Priority Cleanup Admin role to the administrator who creates and manages the policy.

claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Admin is automatically added to Organization Management, allowing its existing members access without a new assignment.
claims.quote: This role is automatically added to the Organization Management role group but must be manually added to any other role group.

claims.claim: The person who last edited the policy cannot also turn it on.
claims.quote: The last person to edit the policy can't also turn it on.

claims.claim: Each item requires at least one other person besides the policy creator to approve deletion.
claims.quote: each item subject to priority cleanup always requires at least one other person to approve the deletion in addition to the person who created the priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: Items under eDiscovery holds also require eDiscovery admin approval.
claims.quote: If an item is also subject to one or more eDiscovery holds, eDiscovery admin approval is also required.

claims.claim: Learn recommends leaving a Priority cleanup policy running for continually created Teams recordings and transcripts.
claims.quote: Because these files are continually created, leave the priority cleanup policy running to automatically find and delete the stale files.

claims.claim: Policy creation fails if the eDiscovery reviewer lacks the correct roles in advance.
claims.quote: If the reviewer for eDiscovery admin doesn't have the correct roles assigned in advance, policy creation fails with an error.

claims.claim: Existing policies continue running after the tenant switch is disabled.
claims.quote: If priority cleanup policies are already created when you turn off the control: Existing priority cleanup policies continue to function

claims.claim: Existing policies cannot be modified while the tenant switch is disabled.
claims.quote: If priority cleanup policies are already created when you turn off the control: Existing priority cleanup policies can't be modified

claims.claim: Approvers must be individual users.
claims.quote: Approvers must be individual users.

claims.quote: Mail-enabled security groups aren't currently supported.

claims.claim: Administrators can monitor permanent deletion by copying the cleanup ID and using it as the audit keyword search string.

claims.claim: Permanent deletion cannot be undone through the recycle bin.
claims.quote: Deleted content bypasses the recycle bins and isn't recoverable under ordinary circumstances. The temporary retention of deleted content doesn't provide a customer-accessible recovery option.
